cards.text: Jesus has just finished telling a whole run of parables. Now He leaves that place and heads to His hometown. And friend, a hometown crowd is a WHOLE different kind of crowd.

cards.question: Back in His hometown, where does Jesus teach the people?
As Jesus teaches in their synagogue, the hometown people are ___.
Listening to Jesus in the synagogue, what are the hometown people asking?

answers.text: Where His wisdom and powers came from
When He will heal the sick in town
How long He plans to stay in town

cards.text: Then the crowd starts listing what they know about Him, like they pulled His whole file. That's a hometown for you: I could roll back in renewed, standing on a gold base, and somebody would STILL say, "Hey, isn't that the 25-cent stamper from the bin?"

cards.question: The hometown crowd calls Jesus the fisherman's son.
The hometown crowd says the name of Jesus's mother is ___.

cards.text: Then they rattle off His brothers like a roll call: James, Joseph, Simon and Judas. They're not asking questions anymore, friend. They're reading the family group chat OUT LOUD.

cards.question: The hometown crowd says all of Jesus's sisters are right there with them.

cards.text: And after all that, they land right back where they started: "Where then did this man get all these things?" They know His mother, His brothers, His sisters, and they STILL can't figure out where it came from.

cards.question: After all their questions, how do the people of His hometown treat Jesus?

answers.text: They ask Him to heal them

cards.text: Jesus answers them with one short line about a prophet and honor. No speech. No long list of His own. One line, and it lands.

cards.question: According to Jesus, where is a prophet without honor?

answers.text: Only in his hometown and his own household
Only in big cities and royal courts

cards.question: In His hometown, Jesus did not do many ___ there, because of their ___.

findings.problem: "They're not asking questions anymore" contradicts the text. The brothers line is still a question ("aren't His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?"), and the crowd keeps asking questions in 13:56, which card 10 itself quotes.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card uses two comparisons, "like a roll call" and "reading the family group chat OUT LOUD." The group chat image also doesn't match the core action, which is naming family members. A group chat isn't a list of names, so the comparison takes a moment to make sense.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card stacks two comparisons, "like they pulled His whole file" and the stamper joke. The joke also calls back to the 25-cent price and the bakery bin. Bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding, but not the bin or the price, and neither has been set up earlier in this lesson.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: "Right there with them" makes it sound like the sisters are standing in the synagogue. The text only asks, "Aren't all His sisters with us as well?", meaning they live among the townspeople. The statement goes further than the text, and it is the statement the baker marks True.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
